method: Each tool's 15 findings were drawn with random.Random(15).sample from raw/t4_findings.json (all findings if fewer than 15; see raw/t4_sample15.json) and read against the source line by one reviewer (the benchmark author, an LLM; subjective). 'correct' = the statement is true of that line and not a pattern the tool itself should recognise as valid.

hadolint.notes: 3 x DL3022 flag `COPY --from=<external image>` which is valid Docker; 10 of 20 Dockerfiles failed to parse at all (DL1000, heredoc RUN <<EOF followed by a comment), so these 15 come only from the 10 parsable files

checksnap --check-docker.notes: all literally true; 5 of 15 are DOC-002 'no USER' on dev-only stages (low value); 4 are DOC-010 (no .dockerignore)

actionlint.notes: all shellcheck SC2086/SC2006 findings inside run: blocks; true but mostly low-risk unquoted ${GITHUB_*} variables

checksnap --check-ci.notes: all literally true; 7 of 15 are INFO/LOW hygiene (ubuntu-latest, no timeout-minutes, no concurrency); 1 HIGH (branch ref release/v1 on pypa publish action, which is that action's documented usage)

yamllint.notes: 15/15 violate default config literally, but 3 are `on:` truthy warnings on GitHub workflows (a well-known false positive) and 4 are line-length on SHA-pinned `uses:` lines that cannot be shortened; 0 of 15 are functional bugs

checksnap --check-config.notes: ALL 12 findings (CFG-003 'Secret in plain text') are `${{ secrets.X }}` / `${{ github.token }}` expression references in GitHub workflows, i.e. the opposite of plain text; only 12 exist so the sample is the whole population

sqlfluff.notes: all style/layout (LT01, LT02, LT05, CV06, CV10); 1 CV06 'must end with a semicolon' on `DELETE FROM store ;` which does end with one; none are bugs

checksnap --check-sql.notes: literally true but 14/15 are SQL-002 DELETE-without-WHERE / SQL-003 DROP-without-IF-EXISTS inside files whose whole purpose is wipe-all / drop-all (sakila *-delete-data.sql, *-drop-objects.sql); only 1 (leading-wildcard LIKE in a CHECK) is a design finding. Corpus is adversarial for these rules
